text:
Updated `ledger/storage.py` to require RFC3339 UTC timestamps with uppercase `T` and a terminal uppercase `Z`. The original timestamp is no longer trimmed, and `datetime` parsing rejects impossible dates and times. Since library writes and stored-record reads use this validator, invalid timestamps are rejected there as well; writes validate all records before opening the ledger, preventing malformed input from causing a partial replacement.

Verified with `python3 -B`: the two specified invalid timestamps and timestamps with surrounding whitespace raise `ValueError`, a valid fractional-second timestamp is accepted, and an invalid stored record is rejected on read. The write check confirmed the existing ledger contents remain unchanged after invalid input. No files beyond `ledger/storage.py` were changed, and the temporary test directory was removed.
